result.scientific_strategy:
## f3356be0-50ce-45d0-a495-b909a50b054c / Scientific strategy

**Current synthesis:** The campaign objective is at least 98% success, or 196/200 episodes, on the official reach-and-hold panel. The fresh baseline reached about 51% development success; reward-credit shaping reached 224/400 pooled success versus 206/400 for its unchanged control; and the subsequent positive-extreme coverage recipe reached 296/400 across two disjoint panels versus 215/400 for its contemporaneous working control. That recipe recovered the positive-extreme sector from 8/65 to 37/65 for the selected checkpoint and reached 73.0% and 75.0% on the two panels. This is meaningful progress but remains far below the official objective. The full reward-plus-coverage recipe is useful under the tested conditions, while the separate causal contributions and reproducibility of the coverage gain remain unresolved.

**Lessons and limits:** Experiment 3's unchanged continuation was near-balanced with its parent and left the positive-extreme sector at zero. Experiment 2's aggressive symmetric sampler reduced overall success and degraded the strong negative-mid sector; experiment 6's gentler balanced sampler also underperformed its parent on a fresh panel and did not improve the negative-extreme sector. These results weaken coverage-only explanations without identifying whether control, representation, hold stability, or optimization is limiting. Experiment 4's reward change improved complete success and mean maximum held duration but increased interruptions and traded angular-sector performance. Experiment 5's positive-extreme focus improved the previously failing sector and measured mid sectors, while negative-extreme success remained 14/69 and its training proxies selected different checkpoints. The positive-extreme result is one transferred training run, although measured on two disjoint panels. Complete uninterrupted hold success is authoritative; proximity, partial hold time, and training reward are incomplete signals. The task-reference panel is reused and selection-contaminated, development panels are not the official verdict, and the unchanged 14-value target-relative observation and 2-value action semantics make the recipe semantically compatible with the same task while not proving that a learned representation transfers or reappears.

**Open questions:** The durability of the positive-extreme coverage gain under fresh initialization is unresolved, as are the causes of the remaining negative-extreme deficit and the durability and causal contribution of the reward direction. It is also unresolved how much learning-process variance affects checkpoint selection and whether any development policy is close to the official 196/200 criterion. No development measurement establishes readiness for terminal assessment.
